title: Drawing consequences is not adding a second rule — Acts prophets
source_text: X. Unde patet rursus hodiernos Sophistas injuste nos vexare, quum aliquod dogma nostrum per bonam consequentiam ex Scriptura eruimus. Quasi in eo retigeremus legem a nobis positam, qua statuimus Scripturam unicam esse fidei & religionis regulam, cui nihil addendum, nihil detrahendum sit. Nam ex Scriptura aliquid deducere non est ei aliquid addere, aut aliam fidei regulam substituere: sed illa ipsa quae continet evolvere, & reconditos ejus thesauros explicare. Ita dicuntur in Actis Prophetae Christo attestari, fore ut qui credit in eum remissionem peccatorum per nomen ejus accipiat. Neque tamen istud ullibi expresse positum, reperitur apud Prophetas; Sed dicuntur Prophetae testari quod ex testimoniis eorum deducitur.
pass_a_gloss: Whence it is plain again that today's Sophists unjustly vex us when we dig out some dogma of ours from Scripture by a good consequence. As if in that we were touching the law laid down by us, by which we establish that Scripture is the unique rule of faith and religion, to which nothing is to be added, nothing taken away. For to deduce something from Scripture is not to add something to it, or to substitute another rule of faith: but to unroll those very things which it contains, and to explain its hidden treasures. Thus in the Acts the Prophets are said to bear witness to Christ, that whoever believes in him receives remission of sins through his name. And yet that is nowhere found expressly set down among the Prophets; but the Prophets are said to testify what is deduced from their testimonies.
pass_b_english: So today's Sophists wrong us when they chide us for drawing a dogma from Scripture by good consequence — as if we broke our own law that Scripture alone is the rule of faith and religion, with nothing added or taken away.
To deduce from Scripture is not to add to it, nor to put another rule in its place. It is to unroll what Scripture already holds and to open its hidden stores.

In Acts the Prophets are said to testify of Christ that whoever believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name. Those bare words are not set down expressly in the Prophets; the Prophets are said to testify what follows from their witness.

choices.why: Mining what is already in the text.

rejected: in Acts as a modern title only
